newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-CHANG ADVANCES IN SAN JOSE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG ADVANCES IN SAN JOSE.

text.p: Second seed Michael Chang painted the lines when he needed to in edging similarly slight and speedy Armenian Sargis Sargsian 6-3 6-4 Thursday to advance to the quarter-finals of the $303,000 Sybase Open.

"He's definitely quick and hits pretty good groundstrokes," said the 5-foot-9 (1.75 metres) Chang about the 5-foot-10 (1.78 metres) Sargsian. "There were times I thought I had put a ball away and I had too hit two or three groundstrokes more to win the point."
Third seed Andre Agassi had a mammoth, two hour and 25 minute struggle against 20-year-old free-swinging Swede Magnus Norman, finally prevailing 4-6 7-6 (7-4) 6-3.
Trading death blows with Norman from the baseline, Agassi found himself on his heels much of the evening.
On Friday, Agassi will play 23-year-old qualifier Grant Doyle of Australia, who reached his first tour quarter-final by beating Jeff Tarango 6-4 7-5.

Chang, a two-time Grand Slam singles finalist in 1996 who ended the year ranked second in the world, said that despite many observers belief that he cannot be the top player, he will continue to battle. "It's part of my character to stand up to the challenge," Chang said.
In Friday's quarter-finals, Chang will face seventh seed Greg Rusedski of Britain, who also advanced to the quarter-finals by firing 17 aces past Canada's Daniel Nestor in a 6-3 6-3 victory.
Chang said the big-serving Rusedski, who is ranked 39th, still has the potential to turn into an elite player.

"Greg has a great deal of talent," Chang said. "His serve is still the one shot that stands out, but he's still pretty young and can improve other parts of his game. He's a very dangerous player that I have lost to in the past and he's not someone to take lightly."
Fourth seed Todd Martin appears headed toward semifinal showdown with friend Pete Sampras. On Thursday, Martin served the lights out in defeating American veteran Jim Grabb 6-3 7-6 (7-5).
On Friday, Martin will sixth seed Richey Reneberg of the United States, who fought off four match points in beating compatriot Jonathan Stark 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (9-7).

Martin, who achieved notoriety last year when he failed to close out MaliVai Washington up 5-1 in the fifth set in the Wimbledon semifinals, said he needs to improve his mental toughness in order to challenge the game's elite.
"I have to learn when to push the accelerator, when to relax, when to increase my intensity, and when to let out what I'm feeling," said the 14th-ranked Martin. "And I need to know how to win ugly."
Top seed Pete Sampras will meet American Chris Woodruff on Friday. Woodruff, the eighth seed, took out Brett Steven of New Zealand 6-3 4-6 6-3.
